Let
\[
\alpha=M e^{i\theta},\qquad \beta=M e^{i\phi}
\]
with \(\theta,\phi\in\mathbb R\). If \(M=0\), then \(\alpha=\beta=0\), which gives \(100=0\), impossible. Thus \(M>0\).

Set
\[
u=\frac{\theta+\phi}{2},\qquad v=\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
\alpha\beta=M^2e^{2iu},\qquad \alpha+\beta=2M\cos v\,e^{iu}.
\]
The condition becomes
\[
M^2e^{2iu}+2M\cos v\,e^{iu}+100=0.
\]
Dividing by \(e^{iu}\),
\[
M^2e^{iu}+2M\cos v+100e^{-iu}=0.
\]
Writing \(e^{iu}=x+iy\), we get
\[
(M^2+100)x+2M\cos v+i(M^2-100)y=0.
\]
Hence the imaginary part gives
\[
(M^2-100)y=0.
\]

If \(M\neq 10\), then \(y=0\), so \(e^{iu}=\pm1\). The real part then gives
\[
|\cos v|=\frac{M^2+100}{2M}.
\]
But
\[
\frac{M^2+100}{2M}>\frac{2M}{2M}=1
\]
because \(M^2-2M+100=(M-1)^2+99>0\). This contradicts \(|\cos v|\le1\).

Therefore \(M=10\). This value is attainable: take
\[
\alpha=-10,\qquad \beta=10.
\]
Then \(|\alpha|=|\beta|=10\) and
\[
\alpha\beta+\alpha+\beta+100=-100-10+10+100=0.
\]

Thus the only possible value is
\[
\boxed{10}
\]
